# Brief: Fire Truck Hero (`fire-truck-hero`)

Read `docs/build/CLOUD.md` first. This brief is the whole contract for your game; the guide it points to holds the rules.

## The game

- Key: `fire-truck-hero`. Name: Fire Truck Hero. Age band: 2 to 4. Emoji: 🚒.
- Generator: `npm run new:game -- fire-truck-hero "Fire Truck Hero" 2-4 🚒`
- Branch: `lane/fire-truck-hero`. Base branch: `feat/learning-games-build`. Base commit: the one your starting message names.
- Subject and the skill that is the verb: Science: what water does to different things.
- Suggested renderer: three.js ("Canvas or three.js" in the guide decides what follows from it). Say in the sheet if you choose otherwise, and why.
- The demo it comes from: `lab/arcade/protos/fire-truck-hero/`. Read it for the idea, the verb and the feel in the hand. Copy no line of it.

## The idea

A toy fire truck with a hose the child aims. Water does a different true thing to each thing it meets: it puts out a small friendly fire, fills a paddling pool, makes a seed sprout, darkens dry ground, floats a boat, spins a wheel, and annoys the cat. Every spray is answered and nothing is a dead end. The fires are never frightening and nobody is in danger. This is not Muddy Truck Wash: there, one routine with tools; here, one tool meeting many materials. The ledger lists the second look for ages four and up: if you fall back to it, your spike must show that it is clear at age two.

The owner's bar for every game: lively and funny, never slow or quiet; animated, cute and warm; deep enough to come back to for weeks through combinations and characters; with no score, coin, streak, reward, praise or timer that pushes. Short animated scenes are welcome where the guide allows them.

## The looks reserved for it, in order

2. Cardboard craft (demo: `box-fort`)

## The records the skill rests on

These were read from the education pack on 2026-10-02. They are where your sheet's records part starts, not the part itself: read each record file and its Limits, check each one again with `npm run -s education:find -- --id <pack id>`, drop one that does not carry your verb, and add one that does. The sheet names no school skill without a record. The skill line at the top of this brief is the wording of the roster; where the Notes below say the records carry less or carry it in another subject, your sheet follows the records, and its claim says only what they carry.

### us-ca
- `edu.us-ca.infant-toddler.science.objective.cognitive-development-strand-1-0-exploration-1-1` (code 1.1): standing department-published-foundation; check state confirmed; level infant-toddler (age 2), basis official. Asks, in our words: a toddler makes easy guesses about what an action will bring about and thinks back over why something happened. Limits the game takes: the guess need not be right; no materials or events are named.
- `edu.us-ca.preschool-tk.science.objective.science-strand-1-0-science-and-engineering-practices-1-5` (code 1.5): standing department-published-foundation; check state confirmed; level preschool-tk (ages 3 to 4), basis official. Asks, in our words: a child says what they think will happen, gives an easy reason, and finds out by trying it. Limits the game takes: adult support is stated for the check (Early) and for planning it (Later), not for the guess; no topic is named; talking about why it came out as it did is only beginning in the Later statement.
- `edu.us-ca.preschool-tk.science.objective.science-strand-2-0-physical-science-2-3` (code 2.3): standing department-published-foundation; check state confirmed; level preschool-tk (ages 3 to 4), basis official. Asks, in our words: a child explores how things and materials change (texture, shape, colour, temperature as examples) and says what changed. Limits the game takes: explore and describe at 3 to 4½, explaining only in the Later statement; the examples are examples.
- `edu.us-ca.preschool-tk.science.objective.science-strand-3-0-life-science-3-7` (code 3.7): standing department-published-foundation; check state confirmed; level preschool-tk (ages 3 to 4), basis official. Asks, in our words: a child knows plants and animals have to be looked after and is starting to see that food and water help living things grow and stay alive. Limits the game takes: at 3 to 4½ feeding and watering are the two things named and the understanding is still forming; a wider list of needs is only in the Later statement.
- `edu.us-ca.preschool-tk.science.objective.science-strand-4-0-earth-and-space-science-4-1` (code 4.1): standing department-published-foundation; check state confirmed; level preschool-tk (ages 3 to 4), basis official. Asks, in our words: a child explores earth materials (water, sand, soil, rocks and air are the examples at the earlier age) and says what they are like. Limits the game takes: describing what a material is like; comparing materials only in the Later statement; nothing on what water does to another material.

### nl
- `edu.nl.peuters.science.objective.inhoudskaart-orientatie-op-jezelf-en-de-wereld-peuters-verschijnselen-uit-natuurkunde-en-techniek-natuurkundige-verschijnselen-2` (code Natuurkundige verschijnselen / 2): standing curriculum-institute-guidance; check state confirmed; level peuters (ages 2 to 3, and a child just turned 4), basis convention. Asks, in our words: discovering and wondering about light, sound, warmth, force (of water and of magnets) and a lamp. Limits the game takes: discovering and wondering only; no explaining; of water it names only its force; it states no safety condition for warmth.
- `edu.nl.peuters.science.objective.inhoudskaart-orientatie-op-jezelf-en-de-wereld-peuters-verschijnselen-uit-natuurkunde-en-techniek-materialen-stoffen-en-voorwerpen-1` (code Materialen, stoffen en voorwerpen / 1): standing curriculum-institute-guidance; check state confirmed; level peuters (ages 2 to 3, and a child just turned 4), basis convention. Asks, in our words: experimenting with safe materials, substances and objects. Limits the game takes: bounded by the word safe, with no list of what is safe; no question to answer and no result to reach.
- `edu.nl.peuters.mathematics.objective.inhoudskaart-rekenen-wiskunde-peuters-meten-meetkunde-meten-inhoud-2` (code Inhoud / 2): standing curriculum-institute-guidance; check state confirmed; level peuters (ages 2 to 3, and a child just turned 4), basis convention. Asks, in our words: gaining experience with how much things hold by filling, pouring over and emptying, water and sand among the examples. Limits the game takes: three actions; no measures and no counting of scoops. It is a mathematics record.
- `edu.nl.fase-1.science.objective.inhoudskaart-orientatie-op-jezelf-en-de-wereld-fase-1-planten-dieren-en-de-mens-groeien-bloeien-en-voortplanten-1` (code Groeien, bloeien en voortplanten / 1): standing curriculum-institute-guidance; check state confirmed; level fase-1 (age 4, groep 1), basis convention. Asks, in our words: realising that plants, animals and people need water, food and a place in order to live. Limits the game takes: a realisation, not an explanation; air, light and warmth are not mentioned; what a school offers in groep 1 and 2.

### Notes
- Thinnest support: age 2 in us-ca (the one cause-and-effect record), and "water makes it grow" for Dutch two- and three-year-olds: the peuter record with the same sub-heading (`edu.nl.peuters.science.objective.inhoudskaart-orientatie-op-jezelf-en-de-wereld-peuters-planten-dieren-en-de-mens-groeien-bloeien-en-voortplanten-1`, confirmed) is experiencing that plants grow and flower, and its Limits says what a plant needs is not mentioned. Keep each outcome a plain cause and effect that needs no explanation.
- No record here is other than `confirmed`.
- Not carried by any record in either jurisdiction: putting out a fire (no record names fire or burning; the only fire in these lanes is the drill in us-ca health 2.6, a safety routine, not water science), wetting, and washing something away. Carried: guessing and seeing what happens (us-ca 1.1, 1.5), a material changing (us-ca 2.3), water as a material (us-ca 4.1; nl Materialen / 1), filling (nl Inhoud / 2, in mathematics), watering helps things grow (us-ca 3.7; nl from fase 1 only), the force of water (nl). Narrow the claim to cause and effect with water, with growing and filling as the two outcomes the records name; fire is the game's story, not its school skill.

## This run

This run covers the design, the look, the toy and the rules. The template you start from is its second version, which holds what the first three.js game (Muddy Truck Wash) learned in a running game, so you build your toy in this run.

1. The steps under "Getting the code" in the cloud page.
2. The design sheet, pushed with `Open: sheet ready for check, round 1`.
3. The look spike for your first reserved look: the game's real scene in the style, at the quality bar, shown by the Mount at load with a fixed seed.
4. The toy: the one action the finger performs most, in the look, with its sound and motion, answered when the finger lands.
5. The rules as pure modules with tests beside them (no renderer, no DOM), in new files of your own, leaving the copied template files as they are wherever you can: the model of the world, the object-by-action grid, the errors as consequences, the characters' tastes, the designed order with its position ids in `config.ts`, the saved state with its defensive `deserialize`, and the size test. The guide lets a remote builder write rules while the check of its sheet runs, at its own risk: record in the status block the sheet commit they were written against.
6. Stop there: write the status block, push, and report. Do not build the game on the toy yet: the owner sees every toy first, and your next message brings the checker's report on your sheet and his answer on your look and your toy.
